cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses with a message for the Israelites. They are to present His food offerings at the appointed time, as a pleasing aroma to Him. Friend, I run six ovens on timers, so when God says "appointed time," I sit up STRAIGHT.
First on the list: two year-old male lambs with no blemish. One lamb is offered in the morning.

cards.question: The first lamb is offered in the morning. When is the second lamb offered?
The LORD wants this pair of lambs offered every day, not just on feast days.

cards.text: Each lamb comes with fine flour mixed with olive oil and a drink offering, every amount measured out. Friend, that's a RECIPE, and I am taking NOTES.

cards.question: This daily burnt offering isn't brand new. The LORD says it was established at Mount ___.

cards.text: Then comes the Sabbath day. Two unblemished year-old lambs go up, with a grain offering and a drink offering.

cards.question: On the Sabbath, those two lambs take the place of the regular daily offering.

cards.text: At the beginning of every month, the list grows: two young bulls, one ram and seven lambs, each with its own grain offering. Friend, that's not an offering, that's a PARADE.

cards.question: This monthly offering is tied to something in the sky. When is it made?
Each month, one male ___ is also presented to the LORD as a sin offering.

cards.text: Now the yearly calendar kicks in. The fourteenth day of the first month is the LORD's Passover.

cards.question: The day after Passover, a seven-day feast begins. What is eaten for all seven days?
On the first day of this feast, Israel holds a sacred assembly and does no regular work.

cards.text: Every day of the feast: two young bulls, one ram, seven lambs and a male goat as a sin offering to make atonement. All of it on top of the regular morning offering, seven days in a row, and NOBODY gets to hit snooze.

cards.question: The feast reaches its seventh and final day. What does Israel hold that day?

cards.text: Next is the day of firstfruits, during the Feast of Weeks. Sacred assembly, no regular work.

cards.question: It's called the day of firstfruits. That day, Israel presents an offering of new ___ to the LORD.

cards.text: Same lineup again, two bulls, a ram, seven lambs and a goat to make atonement, and every animal must be unblemished. I spent years in a junk drawer, friend, so trust me, I know EXACTLY where the dented ones end up.
Now the seventh month, and its first day gets a sacred assembly with no regular work. But this day comes with its own sound.

cards.question: The first day of the seventh month is a day for Israel to sound the ___.

cards.text: The offering: one young bull this time, one ram, seven lambs and a male goat as a sin offering to make atonement.

cards.question: Since this day is also the start of a month, its offering replaces the monthly one.

cards.text: On the tenth day of this seventh month, another sacred assembly. And this time it's not just no regular work, it's no work at ALL.

cards.question: On the tenth day of the seventh month, the Israelites are to ___ themselves.

cards.text: The offering is one young bull, one ram, seven lambs and a goat for a sin offering, on top of the sin offering of atonement. Then on the fifteenth day comes another sacred assembly, and a feast to the LORD begins.

cards.question: The feast after Passover ran seven days. How long does this feast in the seventh month last?

cards.text: Day one, and the numbers EXPLODE: thirteen young bulls, two rams, fourteen lambs and a goat for a sin offering. Thirteen BULLS, friend, and I run six ovens on my busiest day and still need a nap.
Each day after that brings the same two rams, fourteen lambs and goat with their offerings, but one fewer bull: twelve, then eleven, all the way down to seven on the seventh day.

cards.question: When the feast's seven days are done, Israel goes right back to regular work the next day.

cards.text: The eighth day is a solemn assembly, and the offering is one bull, one ram, seven lambs and a goat for a sin offering. Then the LORD sums it up: present these offerings at your appointed times, and friend, this calendar is FULL.

cards.question: These scheduled offerings aren't the only ones. What do they come in addition to?
Moses tells the Israelites all of this, just as the LORD commanded him.

findings.problem: Moses shows up here for the first time in the lesson, but the card never says who he is. It just says "the LORD speaks to Moses."

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question says these offerings "aren't the only ones," so the baker is looking for more offerings. "Their vow and freewill offerings" is the only answer that names offerings. "Tithes and harvest taxes" and "gifts for the Levites" don't. "Harvest taxes" also sounds more modern than the other two answers. The right answer can be picked from the wording alone.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Almost the whole passage (Numbers 28:3-29:39) is rules for offerings and feasts, which is listed as a long stretch. The long-stretch rule says a stretch gets one summary story card, never a choice card, and never a stop of its own. Here the stretch is the entire passage, so it fills two stops and has many choice cards on offering details. Examples are the male goat each month (stop 1, card 11), the new moon (stop 1, card 10) and the sacred assembly on the seventh day (stop 1, card 16). The docs don't say what to do when a whole passage is a long stretch. "A short passage does what it can" doesn't settle it either. The feast calendar might also count as "key laws," which are not long stretches.
findings.question: When a whole passage is a long stretch, like the offering and feast rules in Numbers 28-29, should Prep be one summary story card with no choice cards? Or should the calendar of appointed times (daily, Sabbath, monthly, Passover, Weeks, the seventh-month days) count as key laws that get story and choice cards, with only the amounts and the day-by-day repeats summed up? And how many stops and cards should a passage like this get?
